source_scope: Diseases of Swine, 11th Edition, pages 1-200 markdown extraction
note: These are paraphrased operational facts derived from the first 200 pages. They should be reviewed before insertion into exports/knowledge_facts.json.

candidate_facts.subject: swine herd case evaluation
candidate_facts.object: Swine disease diagnosis should use herd stage, group pattern, history, records, site observations, and individual pig findings before final interpretation.

candidate_facts.subject: swine farm user_query
candidate_facts.object: A realistic swine farm question should include production stage, group size, onset, spread, management context, and prior interventions when relevant.

candidate_facts.subject: swine disease diagnosis
candidate_facts.object: Clinical signs, history, lesions, laboratory results, and epidemiology should be interpreted together rather than treating one sign or one test as definitive.

candidate_facts.subject: pathogen detection
candidate_facts.object: Detection of an organism should be interpreted with clinical compatibility, lesions, timing, and differential diagnosis before assigning causality.

candidate_facts.subject: swine diagnostic sampling
candidate_facts.object: Sample type and animal selection should be driven by the syndrome, the diagnostic question, lesion distribution, and whether the sampled animals represent the active problem.

candidate_facts.subject: diagnostically representative animals
candidate_facts.object: Sampling should prioritize animals that represent the current active disease process; untreated or early cases are often more diagnostically useful when available.

candidate_facts.subject: reproductive failure sampling
candidate_facts.object: Reproductive failure investigations should consider fetal, placental, and sow or gilt samples together with herd history and timing.

candidate_facts.subject: swine necropsy
candidate_facts.object: Postmortem examination can support diagnosis when external and internal findings are recorded and tissues are collected safely for appropriate tests.

candidate_facts.subject: swine disease control
candidate_facts.object: Control planning should consider host susceptibility, pathogen transmission and persistence, environmental pressure, and management routes of spread.

candidate_facts.subject: swine farm biosecurity
candidate_facts.object: Biosecurity assessment should consider live animal movement, dead pig handling, transport routes, feed and ingredient delivery, people, clothing, footwear, equipment, and shared tools.

candidate_facts.subject: swine drug therapy
candidate_facts.object: Drug therapy should start with a defined objective and should account for production logistics, regulation, withdrawal and residue responsibility, and outcome reassessment.

candidate_facts.subject: whole-group antimicrobial treatment
candidate_facts.object: Whole-group antimicrobial escalation should not be automatic; it should be justified by diagnosis, risk context, veterinary oversight, and reassessment of response.

candidate_facts.subject: swine food animal drug use
candidate_facts.object: Withdrawal and residue decisions require regulatory and label context and should not be generalized in train-ready disease QA without authoritative label support.

candidate_facts.subject: swine anesthesia and surgical procedures
candidate_facts.object: Anesthesia and surgical protocol details require professional veterinary context and should not be generated as routine disease QA unless explicitly relevant.
